standard_prerequisites.name: Sparsity parameters
standard_prerequisites.statement: A pair of integer sequences K and L, together with an ordered partition of the vertex set into classes, so that every subset of vertices has its edge count bounded by the weighted size of the classes it meets minus the corresponding parameter.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the notion of sparsity under consideration.

standard_prerequisites.name: Support of a graph
standard_prerequisites.statement: The edges of the graph are supported on an initial run of the vertex classes when no edge meets a later class.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: The numbered parameter inequalities
standard_prerequisites.statement: Three inequalities relating consecutive parameter entries, the first ensuring that a single edge is sparse and the others ensuring that sparsity survives adding isolated vertices.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the hypotheses invoked in the proof.

core_obligations: Observe that the forward direction is immediate, since restricting the vertex set cannot create a violating subset (source line 295).

Reduce the converse to showing that sparsity survives adding a set of isolated vertices in one new class, and verify the bound for an arbitrary subset of the enlarged vertex set by splitting according to whether the subset meets later classes (source lines 295-299).

In the case where the subset meets two later classes, take the largest such index and use the first of the numbered inequalities to absorb the two new class contributions into the bound (source lines 301-307).
For the remaining configuration, where the subset meets the last old class and the first later class, use the same inequality to conclude (source lines 307-308).

proof_roadmap.step: The easy direction and the reduction to adding isolated vertices.
Bound a subset that stays inside the old classes.
Handle subsets meeting later classes, using the numbered inequalities.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled lemma at source lines 289-293: for parameters K and L satisfying the three numbered inequalities, if the edges of a graph are supported on the first t of the n vertex classes with t smaller than n, then the graph is sparse for K and L exactly when the graph on those t classes is sparse for the restricted parameters. The author gave it no label, so its position is part of its identity. The proof (source lines 294-308) is a subset-by-subset verification: after the immediate direction it reduces the claim to adding isolated vertices in a new class, and then bounds an arbitrary subset of the enlarged vertex set in three configurations, namely subsets contained in the old classes, subsets meeting two later classes, and subsets meeting the last old class together with a later one; the first numbered inequality is what absorbs the contribution of the later classes in the second and third configurations. The statement records only the equivalence.
